precepts.text: Deacon: the same thing that happened with Paul happened with Christ. After these things Jesus walked in Galilee: for he would not walk in Jewry, because the Jews sought to kill him. He wasn't walking with the southern kingdom no more. And Matthew 4:15 shows you who was in Galilee: Zebulun and Naphtali. So the same thing Paul and Barnabas encountered, with the Jews rejecting salvation in Jesus Christ, is the same thing Christ had to deal with.
precepts.point: The interview with Captain OC: the Christian guy said, back in the day you guys only taught black Americans, but now you're saying the Hispanics and Latinos are the Israelites; what changed? Remember what we read in Zechariah 12:7: I will save who first? Judah. Judah would get the gospel first. It's always been that. Picture shown from the early 80s: Ahrayah with the 12 tribes sign. Prior to this, everybody was primarily just teaching the kingdom of Judah; then the Most High showed Ahrayah about the other tribes.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
“But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with envy, and spake against those things which were spoken by Paul, contradicting and blaspheming.” The same thing that happened with Paul happened with Christ: “After these things Jesus walked in Galilee: for he would not walk in Jewry, because the Jews sought to kill him.”

Christ was not walking with the southern kingdom any more. He went to Galilee, and Matthew 4:15 shows you who was in Galilee: Zebulun and Naphtali, “Galilee of the Gentiles”. Those Gentiles are the northern kingdom.

So the same thing Paul and Barnabas met, the Jews rejecting salvation in Jesus Christ, is the same thing Christ had to deal with. And Paul did what Christ did: “seeing ye put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles.”

The word had to be spoken to Judah “first”, as the Lord “shall save the tents of Judah first”. When Judah put it from them, Christ went into Galilee, and Paul and Barnabas turned to the Gentiles: the northern kingdom. You cannot just assume that because it says Gentiles it means the other nations; there are times it refers to the Israelites in a Gentile state, cut off from being his people in Hosea chapter 1.

precepts.text: I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.
precepts.point: The majority of the masses did not have what we call the Old Testament. It was the learned men that had the parchments, and it was their job to instruct the people. But now God gave it to the apostles to teach.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
“Yet a little while am I with you, and then I go unto him that sent me.” Who sent Jesus? Christ answers it himself: “I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.”

He did not come on his own errand. He was sent from his Father, and he sought only the Father's will. And that will was to gather the twelve tribes of Israel: other sheep he must bring in, that there might be one fold and one shepherd. The gathering began when Christ came and began to teach, and his death was the beginning of the twelve tribes being brought back together.

So when he says he goes “unto him that sent me”, he is going back to the Father whose will he came to do. What that will was, the prophets had already written, and Isaiah 11 shows it.

precepts.text: There shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots: that Branch is Christ; you can read that in Zechariah 6. He shall not judge after the sight of his eyes: the same exact thing he said in John 5:30. So what did God send him to do?
precepts.point: The majority of the masses did not have what we call the Old Testament. It was the learned men that had the parchments, and it was their job to instruct the people. But now God gave it to the apostles to teach.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
The Old Testament shows who was sent and why. “And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots”: that Branch is Christ, as Zechariah 6 shows. “And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord.”

Then: “and he shall not judge after the sight of his eyes, neither reprove after the hearing of his ears.” That is the same exact thing Christ said in John 5:30: “as I hear, I judge”, “I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.” The Branch out of Jesse does not judge by himself; he does the will of the one who sent him.

So what did God send him to do? Keep reading in the same chapter, and verse 12 tells it: to set up an ensign, assemble the outcasts of Israel and gather the dispersed of Judah. When Christ spoke in the New Testament, he was reiterating what the Old Testament already said, and the text substantiates it.

precepts.text: To it shall the Gentiles seek. Who are the Gentiles in this regard? A brother answered: stay in the passage; verses 11 and 12 explain it. The Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, and he shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth. The Gentiles he is talking about are the outcasts of Israel. That was God's will in sending his Son: to gather the twelve tribes.
precepts.point: The majority of the masses did not have what we call the Old Testament. It was the learned men that had the parchments, and it was their job to instruct the people. But now God gave it to the apostles to teach.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
“And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious.” Who are the Gentiles here? The Jews in John 7 asked, “will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?” The answer is Israel, and it is proven by staying in the passage.

“the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea. And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” The Gentiles that seek the root of Jesse are the outcasts of Israel, the remnant of his people.

That was God's will in sending his Son: to gather the twelve tribes of Israel. The Pharisees and chief priests were studied men. They understood this prophecy of the dispersed, which is why they asked whether he would go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles.

precepts.text: Ye shall seek me and shall not find me: when your fear cometh as desolation, then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me.
precepts.point: The majority of the masses did not have what we call the Old Testament. It was the learned men that had the parchments, and it was their job to instruct the people. But now God gave it to the apostles to teach.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
“Ye shall seek me, and shall not find me: and where I am, thither ye cannot come.” The Old Testament already spoke it: “When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you. Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me.”

They will not. The same words Christ spoke to the Pharisees and chief priests are written in Proverbs, against those who would not hear. When Christ, the apostles and the prophets spoke in the New Testament, their conversation was reiterating what the Old Testament was saying, and they could substantiate it with the text.

precepts.text: The reason Isaiah 11 says he shall set up an ensign for the nations is because we were going to be scattered among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other, and live as Gentiles.
precepts.point: The majority of the masses did not have what we call the Old Testament. It was the learned men that had the parchments, and it was their job to instruct the people. But now God gave it to the apostles to teach.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Isaiah 11 says “he shall set up an ensign for the nations”. Why for the nations? Because Israel was going to be scattered: “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

We were going to be scattered in all these nations and live as Gentiles, serving other gods. So the ensign set up for the nations is set up to “assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” The ones he gathers out of the nations are Israel.

That is what the Jews meant in John 7 when they asked, “will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles”? They knew the curse: Israel scattered from one end of the earth to the other.

precepts.text: Israel was delivered for a spoil, unto captivity, unto death, and for a proverb of reproach to all the nations among whom we are dispersed.
precepts.point: The majority of the masses did not have what we call the Old Testament. It was the learned men that had the parchments, and it was their job to instruct the people. But now God gave it to the apostles to teach.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Tobit shows the dispersed are Israel once again: “For they obeyed not thy commandments: wherefore thou hast delivered us for a spoil, and unto captivity, and unto death, and for a proverb of reproach to all the nations among whom we are dispersed.”

Israel disobeyed the commandments, and so was delivered for a spoil, into captivity, unto death, and made a proverb of reproach among all the nations where they were dispersed. The Pharisees understood Tobit and the dispersed, just as they understood Isaiah 11. That is why they said of Christ, “will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?” They knew who the dispersed were.

precepts.text: He will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations among whom he hath scattered us. Again it uses the word nations, explaining that it was Israel being scattered.
precepts.point: The majority of the masses did not have what we call the Old Testament. It was the learned men that had the parchments, and it was their job to instruct the people. But now God gave it to the apostles to teach.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
“And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he hath scattered us.” Again it uses the word nations, explaining that it was Israel being scattered among them.

The scourge is for our iniquities, but mercy comes again, and the promise is the gathering out of all nations. That is the same gathering Isaiah 11 speaks of, and the same work Christ was sent to begin: bringing the dispersed out from among the Gentiles, where they had been scattered.

precepts.text: And I scattered them among the heathen, and they were dispersed through the countries.
precepts.point: The majority of the masses did not have what we call the Old Testament. It was the learned men that had the parchments, and it was their job to instruct the people. But now God gave it to the apostles to teach.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Ezekiel says the same: “And I scattered them among the heathen, and they were dispersed through the countries: according to their way and according to their doings I judged them.”

They're dispersed. Israel was scattered among the heathen and dispersed through the countries, judged according to their own ways and doings. The Pharisees and chief priests understood Ezekiel 36 and the dispersed, along with Isaiah 11 and Tobit 3. So when they asked, “Whither will he go, that we shall not find him? will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?”, they were speaking of scattered Israel living among the heathen.

precepts.text: Paul taught all the Jews which are among the Gentiles. We know from the text that the Jews were going to be dispersed among the Gentiles and live like Gentiles. The New Testament shows Paul going out to find the Jews scattered among the other nations, living like strangers and heathens, and bringing them back to God. The job was to raise up the twelve tribes of Israel again.
precepts.point: The majority of the masses did not have what we call the Old Testament. It was the learned men that had the parchments, and it was their job to instruct the people. But now God gave it to the apostles to teach.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
The New Testament shows the dispersed being taught: “And they are informed of thee, that thou teachest all the Jews which are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs.” There were Jews among the Gentiles, and Paul was going to them.

We know from the text that the Jews were going to be dispersed among the Gentiles and live like Gentiles. Coming back to the New Testament, it shows Paul going out to find the Jews scattered among these other nations, living like Gentiles, living like strangers, living like heathens, and bringing them back to God.

This was the prophecy sent from the Old Testament: the job was to raise up the twelve tribes of Israel again. What the Jews in John 7 asked, “will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles”?, is exactly what was done.

precepts.text: Moses gave unto you circumcision, not because it is of Moses but of the fathers: Abraham's circumcision is not the manner of Moses.
precepts.point: Luke 2 confirms it: eight days accomplished for the circumcising of the child, the days of her purification according to the law of Moses, presented to the Lord with a sacrifice of two turtledoves.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
If circumcision after the manner of Moses is circumcision with sacrifice, is all circumcision of Moses? Christ answers it: “Moses therefore gave unto you circumcision; (not because it is of Moses, but of the fathers;) and ye on the sabbath day circumcise a man.”

Moses gave it to them, but circumcision is not of Moses. It is of the fathers, of Abraham, who was the one first circumcised. So when Acts 15 says circumcised after the manner of Moses, that is not the same thing as the circumcision of Abraham.

There are two different things here: circumcision of the fathers, and circumcision after the manner of Moses with the sacrifice of Leviticus 12 behind it. Seeing that difference is what opens up what the Pharisees were demanding and what Paul was fighting in his letters.

precepts.text: Then said the Jews, whither will he go that we shall not find him? Will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles? The dispersed are Israelites, and the Jews of the circumcision call the dispersed Israelites Gentiles. Now you know who the Gentiles are that Paul writes to.
precepts.point: Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ. Here is where the other gospel and the error of the wicked come in: all you have to do is believe, you can lie, cheat, steal, and rape in the name of Jesus, as a Dominican in the Bronx once told me. Works of the law, law singular, shout out to Captain Zakar: the law of sacrifice from Nehemiah 10:33. A man no longer receives atonement by sacrificial law, for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified. Christians will run to Galatians 2:16, 3:2, and 3:5; these are their go-tos, and I am giving you the tools.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
Paul keeps saying “among”: the gospel “which I preach among the Gentiles”, preaching him “among the heathen”. Why does he keep using that word? Because Israel was scattered among the nations, and that is who he is writing to the entire time. Then he says “the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter”. Christ wrought effectually in Peter toward the Jews born and raised in the law and circumcised the eighth day, “the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles”.

Who are those Gentiles? John answers: “Then said the Jews among themselves, Whither will he go, that we shall not find him? will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?” The Jews here are the circumcision, born and raised in the Mosaic law. They ask where Christ will go that they cannot find him. Will he go to the dispersed? The dispersed are the Israelites, the diaspora scattered among the Gentiles.

And what do the Jews call those dispersed Israelites? Gentiles: “and teach the Gentiles”. So now you know who the Gentiles are that Paul writes to throughout the entire time. It should be a no-brainer now.

That is why James, Cephas and John gave Paul and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship, “that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision”: Paul to the Israelites scattered among the nations, the others to the Jews who were not scattered abroad. And it is why Paul withstood Peter at Antioch. Peter ate with these Gentiles, the scattered Israelites he was teaching who they are, then withdrew when certain came from James, fearing them of the circumcision. You cannot teach the scattered who they are and then act as if you are not with them; that is a bad example.

precepts.text: Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment; the same standard the Most High gave Samuel in this verse.
precepts.point: This still happens today: brothers will look at a group and assume the biggest one must be the leader, not knowing that brother might be the soldier while the leader is the slim one beside him.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

precepts.why:
When Samuel looked on Eliab, he judged through his own lens as a man: “Surely the Lord’s anointed is before him.” The Most High corrected him: “Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him”. Looking the mightiest and the tallest does not make a man the one the Most High picked.

“Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment.” That is the same standard the Most High gave Samuel in this verse: “man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart.”

This still happens today. Brothers will look at a group and assume the biggest one must be the leader, not knowing that brother might be the soldier while the leader is the slim one beside him.

precepts.text: Are ye angry at me, because I have made a man every whit whole on the sabbath day? Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment.
precepts.point: He had broken no sabbath. He answers them elsewhere out of their own practice: they circumcise on the sabbath so that the law of Moses be not broken, and a man made every whit whole is greater than that.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

precepts.why:
The Jews persecuted Jesus and sought to slay him, “because he had done these things on the sabbath day.” He had broken no sabbath. He answers them elsewhere out of their own practice: “Moses therefore gave unto you circumcision; (not because it is of Moses, but of the fathers;) and ye on the sabbath day circumcise a man.”

“If a man on the sabbath day receive circumcision, that the law of Moses should not be broken; are ye angry at me, because I have made a man every whit whole on the sabbath day?” They circumcise on the sabbath so that the law of Moses be not broken, and a man made every whit whole is greater than that.

“Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment.” By the appearance, he worked on the sabbath; by righteous judgment, he made a man whole, and that broke no sabbath.

precepts.text: Out of the believer's belly shall flow rivers of living water; this he spake of the Spirit, for the Holy Ghost was not yet given because Jesus was not yet glorified.
precepts.point: John said he must decrease and Christ must increase, and that happens in increments. Two of John's own disciples heard Christ and followed him, which is why in Acts the disciples were still baptizing with water even though Christ himself baptized not with water but with the Holy Ghost. When you believe on Christ as the scripture says, rivers of living water flow out of your belly, meaning wisdom and understanding flow out of the mind that consumes and filters information; but that Holy Ghost was not yet given because Jesus was not yet glorified.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.”

When you believe on Christ as the scripture says, rivers of living water flow out of your belly. That means wisdom and understanding flow out of the mind, the part that consumes and filters information.

“But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive: for the Holy Ghost was not yet given; because that Jesus was not yet glorified.” That is why they were to be baptized with the Holy Ghost “not many days hence.” It could not come until he was glorified.

precepts.text: His brethren told him to depart and show himself to the world, for neither did his brethren believe in him at that time.
precepts.point: "His brethren" are Christ's own brothers. During his ministry they did not believe in him and told him to go show himself openly in Judaea, but after his death and the miracles they came to believe. James the Just, the Lord's brother, became an apostle and was later killed.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
During his ministry his own brothers did not believe in him. “His brethren therefore said unto him, Depart hence, and go into Judea, that thy disciples also may see the works that thou doest.” They told him, “If thou do these things, shew thyself to the world. For neither did his brethren believe in him.”

But after his death and the miracles they came to believe. That is why the same brethren who doubted him are found in the upper room, continuing with one accord in prayer and supplication.

precepts.text: The Jews marvelled that he knew letters, having never learned, and Christ answered that his doctrine is not his own but his that sent him, and whoever will do his will shall know the doctrine.
precepts.point: Peter was fearless and intrepid, a man who drew a sword and cut off the man's ear, which was not the first time he used it; he came from the streets, and we have brothers with that same posture. They took knowledge the disciples had been with Christ because you take on the attributes and characteristics of whoever you surround yourself with, and the disciples all spoke the same thing as Christ.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
The rulers marvelled at Christ the same way they marvelled at Peter and John: “How knoweth this man letters, having never learned?” His answer: “My doctrine is not mine, but his that sent me. If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself.”

The rulers saw that Peter and John were not slick, cunning and crafty like themselves. They were bold, unlearned and ignorant men, coming as if straight off a plantation and a field, not the regular church men. That boldness is the natural animation of the Holy Spirit, not something you force or make up. If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine.

precepts.text: The Jews ask whether Christ will go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles and teach the Gentiles, meaning the scattered of Israel.
precepts.point: It says "the Jew first, and also the Gentile" because prophecy set Judah, Benjamin, and Levi to rise up first, and the "Gentiles" are the dispersed northern tribes scattered among the heathen, left few in number. This is the diaspora, the same scattering some now call the African diaspora.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Then said the Jews among themselves, Whither will he go, that we shall not find him? will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?”

The dispersed among the Gentiles are the scattered of Israel. When the Jews asked whether Christ would go and teach the Gentiles, they meant Israelites dispersed among the nations. That is who the Gentiles are in Peter's word: the northern tribes in the diaspora.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 15 The Seven Last Plagues

precepts.why: “Will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?” The dispersed are the scattered Israelites; they called the scattered Israelites Gentiles. They were not a people.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 15 The Seven Last Plagues

precepts.why: “Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment.” Go by what the Bible says. When you go by your eyes you go, that’s my friend, I like him; that’s my sister, I love her. Many of those that fell out of this congregation judged according to appearance. Righteous judgment means what does the law say: go to your brother or sister one on one, not social media.
